findings.text: Raw IPv6 socket state starts with generic internet socket state followed by checksum control, checksum offset, ICMPv6 filter, multicast table identifier, drop accounting and IPv6 private options. UDP and TCP IPv6 objects each contain only their base transport state plus the same IPv6 private options area.

The generic socket member must stay first inside the raw IPv6 object so generic and raw pointers remain interchangeable. The IPv6 timewait object carries only one generic TCP timewait member and nothing else shown.

Two builds of the IPv6 helpers are shown. The enabled build gates on a global disable flag, returns stored private state for full sockets and null otherwise, derives enclosing raw state from embedded state, reads the v6 only flag, tests family plus receive option bits, returns the stored receive address for v6 family and null otherwise, and handles timewait and normal sockets uniformly. The disabled build collapses all gates and lookups to constant false, zero or null.

Callers use a guarded private lookup for full sockets, a container derivation from embedded generic state to raw state, a family checked receive address fetch, and a uniform v6 only query across normal and timewait sockets.
The ISA DMA bridge bug indicator has value 0. The boot firmware table window begins at 0x80000 and ends at 0x100000.
A firmware table reservation helper is provided as an empty inline with no effect in the shown build. Inclusion guards mark the ISA DMA, boot firmware, inode version and journaling headers as seen.
The queried shift is 1, giving a queried flag of 1 and an increment step of 2. Logical versions live above the shift while low bits carry bookkeeping.

Version handling offers direct raw store, shifted logical store, shifted store with queried marking, monotonic raise that loops until the stored value reaches at least the target, forced increment, direct raw increment, queried pending test and equality comparison against a snapshot.
Time conversion packs seconds into the high half and nanoseconds into the low half of one 64 bit attribute word.

Out of memory retry is 1, default max commit age is 5, minimum journal length is 1024 blocks, default fast commit size is 256 blocks, batch size is 64, replay stop is 0, replay continue is 1, and on disk magic is 0xc03b3998.

Block types are 1 descriptor and 2 commit and 3 first superblock and 4 second superblock and 5 revoke. Checksum kinds are 1 CRC32 and 2 MD5 and 3 SHA1 and 4 CRC32C with CRC32 width 4 and array length defined as 32 divided by width of a 32 bit word. Tag flags are 1 escape and 2 same identifier and 4 deleted and 8 last tag.

Compatible checksum is 0x1. Incompatible bits are revoke 0x1 and 64 bit 0x2 and async commit 0x4 and checksum v2 0x8 and checksum v3 0x10 and fast commit 0x20. Known compatible keeps only checksum while known read only compatible is empty and known incompatible unions all six. Internal positions are 0 commit running and 1 write data and 2 wait data with masks as one shifted by each position. Recovery passes are scan then revoke then replay.

Common header holds magic plus type plus sequence as big endian words. Commit record adds checksum kind plus size plus pad plus checksum array plus commit seconds plus nanoseconds. Current tags hold number plus flags plus high bits plus checksum as wide words while older tags use narrower middle pair for checksum and flags. Tails hold one checksum word and revoke blocks pair common header with used count.

Superblock version two orders common header first and geometry next and log state next and error next and three feature words next and a sixteen byte journal identifier next and sharing plus dynamic copy next and transaction limits next and checksum kind next and fast commit size plus clean head next and pad plus trailing checksum next and a large user area last, filling one kilobyte with documented group offsets.
Public aliases expose the atomic handle type and the journal control type while hiding underlying structure tags.

Transactions advance from T_RUNNING through T_LOCKED and T_SWITCH and T_FLUSH into T_COMMIT with T_COMMIT_DFLUSH plus T_COMMIT_JFLUSH plus T_COMMIT_CALLBACK before reaching T_FINISHED. Only the background journal thread moves this field, with list protection needed when entering finished before release.

Transaction control joins journal link plus identifier plus state plus log start plus buffer count plus five buffer lists plus inode list plus wait and start timing plus request time plus checkpoint stats plus atomic update and credit and revoke and handle counts plus checkpoint queue links plus expiry plus start time plus sync flag plus flush need. Checkpoint stats track time plus forced close plus written plus dropped while run stats add phase durations and handle plus block totals.

Atomic handles join a transaction or journal link plus reserved link plus credit totals plus revoke accounting plus reference plus error plus sync and reserved and aborted and invalid marks plus type plus line plus start plus requested credits plus allocation context. Journaled inodes join current plus next transaction links plus list node plus constant VFS link plus flags plus a page indexed dirty span that counts empty when start meets or passes end.

Journal control starts with flags plus error plus abort exclusion plus superblock buffer pair plus state lock plus barrier count plus barrier exclusion plus running plus committing plus checkpoint links plus six wait queues for locked commit and done commit and commit trigger and updates and reserved credits and fast commit plus checkpoint exclusion and pending list, with tail beyond shown window unseen.

List lock guards inode links and lists and flags and dirty span and most transaction buffer lists and inode lists and checkpoint queueing and finished entry. State lock guards journal scalars and barrier counts and running plus committing pointers and request time. Handle fields and journal link plus identifier plus expiry need no locking. Buffer head pinning uses a dedicated bit spin with paired acquire and release around private access.

Dirty queries sample start and end once and report empty when start reaches or passes end, else map pages to inclusive bytes by shifting and decrementing the upper edge by one. Time gaps subtract directly when ordered else wrap via max offset. Buffer and head convert through paired private pointers with generated per bit helpers.

Assertions abort on false while expectations either assert or log function plus expression plus reason and yield the value, so logging builds do not abort. Debug calls either forward file plus function plus line to an internal logger or sink to a no op printer by build. Expensive checking and debug selection change these paths.
Small utilities translate between buffer and head, bracket journal head access with bit lock pair, fetch dirty byte spans with empty signalling, and compute wrapped jiffy deltas.

Buffer bits progress from attachment at private start through writeout and freed and revoked and revoke valid and dirty and head pin and shadow and verified toward a private reuse base, with per bit test plus set plus clear plus test and set allowing non linear moves like dirtying plus revoking plus shadowing.

Leading the raw socket with anything but generic state breaks interchange. Monotonic raises must retry compare exchange and must not assume one shot success. Multibyte disk fields are big endian and need conversion on little hosts, and mixing superblock versions truncates feature plus identifier plus checksum coverage.
